page.layout: One page of text, verse. Top: continuation of a hymn in italic verse, seven stanzas set as pairs of lines. Below a rule: a centred heading "CANTICVM SIMEONIS." then a stanza with a large initial N. Right-aligned attributions "Sc. S." and "IDEM" at the foot. Running head at top centre, page number at top left.

p.i: Cuius amica piis clementia semper aperta eft, Pertribuit magnus munera magna mihi. Ille potens, terra stupeat qua maximus orbis, Ingenti manuum robore multa facit.
Vana quibus nimio turgescunt pectora fastu, Deiectos animi spe iubet esse sui.
Cum lubet, elatos solio deturbat ab alto: Cum lubet, abiectos ad loca summa vehit.
Hoc ditatur inops, modo quem fors dura premebat: Hoc fit inanis opum, qui modo plenus erat.
Ille etiam Abrahamo, veterisque nepotibus olim Abrahami certa quod dedit ante fide,
Israele satos iuvat, æternumque iuvabit Quem populum in tempus vendicat omne sibi.

Nunc (quod ante receperas futurum) Nunc tibi, Deus ô benigne, tandem Dimittor placida quiete felix. Cum tuo famulo tuam Salutem Hisce luminibus datur tueri. Hanc in luce palam exhibes aperta Nationibus omnibus videndam, Lumen gentibus aureum prophanis, Æternum Solimis tuis honorem.

page.notes: The initial N of "Nunc" is a large woodcut-style capital, read as N followed by "Vnc". Some letters in the last line, "Solimis tuis", are damaged and "tuis" is doubtful; the initial of "Æternum" is partly obscured. The scan is slightly blurred with show-through from the reverse page, which was not transcribed.
